Swampscott Civic Digest — week ending 2026-11-20

Meetings this week

Planning Board, 2026-11-16

  • Source: Transcript, Agenda
  • Attendance: Joseph Sheridan (Chair), Jer Jurma, Ariane Purdy, Bill Quinn.
  • Petition 26-14 (8 Palmer Avenue): Approved a Site Plan Special Permit for garage and interior/exterior additions. The project increases open space by approximately 6% by replacing a concrete patio with pervious gravel.
  • Petition 26-15 (487 Humphrey Street): Continued to December 14. The board requested significant revisions to site safety and design, specifically regarding egress, dumpster enclosure, utility screening, and landscaping/buffering to protect the neighbor. The board expressed safety concerns about side doors/stoops opening directly into a narrow drive aisle.
  • Administrative: Approved the 2027 meeting and submittal schedule.

Select Board, 2026-11-18

  • Source: Transcript, Agenda
  • Attendance: Katie Phelan (Chair), Danielle Leonard (Vice Chair), MaryEllen Fletcher, Ted Dooley, Wayne Spritz.
  • Trash & Recycling: Town Administrator Connors announced a transition to a "toter-tipper" collection system and a shift to every-other-week recycling pickup starting January 2027.
  • Parking: Approved resident-only parking (year-round) for Ingalls Terrace and the entirety of Cedar Hill Terrace, with specific "No Parking" zones for safety.
  • Labor Agreements: Approved Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) for AFSCME 2610 (DPW) and SEIU 888 (Library).
  • Governance: Formally adopted the town website as the official posting location for public meetings.
  • Disability Commission: Approved increasing the commission's membership from 5 to 7 to manage workload.
  • Tax Classification: Opened the public hearing on FY2027 tax rates; hearing continued to December 2 as official state certification is pending.

Planning Board, 2026-11-09

  • Source: Transcript
  • Attendance: Bill Quinn (Acting Chair), Jer Jurma, Ariane Purdy. (Note: Board was short on members, forcing the continuation of several items).
  • Petitions: Continued Petition 26-11 (45 Pleasant St) to December 14; continued Petitions 26-14 and 26-15 to the November 16 special meeting.
  • Zoning Amendments: Tabled two proposed zoning articles (codification and state law alignment) as they did not make the December town meeting warrant; they will be revisited for the Spring Annual Town Meeting.
  • Citizen's Petition (Tom Bogacz): Held a public hearing for an amendment to align medical marijuana zoning with state law, permitting standalone medical retail stores. The board voted to recommend favorable action at Town Meeting, with a suggested amendment to require a Special Permit for facilities between 2,000–10,000 sq. ft. in B-3 and B-4 districts.

Connections to town planning documents

  • Select Board (11/18): Discussed the PACE program for energy efficiency, connecting to Buildings & Energy 2.2.B (C-PACE program) in the Climate Action & Resilience Plan.
  • Planning Board (11/09): The marijuana zoning amendment relates to LU-S041 (recodifying the zoning bylaw) and ED-G03 (support mixed-use development) in the Master Plan 2035.
  • Select Board (11/18): Parking changes relate to TR-G04 (manage traffic & parking) and PF-S012 (sidewalk/overgrowth) in the Master Plan 2035.

Coming up next week

  • Finance Committee: 2026-11-23 (December warrant articles, 2028 forecast, FY27 tax rate analysis).
  • Solid Waste Advisory Committee: 2026-11-23 (Trash contract roll-out updates, school composting audit).
  • Retirement Board: 2026-11-24 (Financial reports, 2027 budget).

Board & committee membership changes

  • Martha Schmitt on Master Plan Committee: role changed from Climate Action Plan Committee Rep to Renewable Energy Rep
  • Edward “Ted” Dooley on Master Plan Committee: role changed from Planning Board Rep to Harbor & Waterfront Committee Rep
  • Martha Schmitt on Master Plan Committee: role changed from Renewable Energy Rep to Climate Action Plan Committee Rep
  • Edward “Ted” Dooley on Master Plan Committee: role changed from Harbor & Waterfront Committee Rep to Planning Board Rep
